sermon.title: The End Time Judgment, Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues the series on the end-time judgment, explaining that God instituted government by law, that Jesus’ first coming was to warn and save and His second is to judge by works, that even believers will appear before the judgment seat of Christ, and that the new heaven and earth have levels of reward.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he says “Matthew 16:20” (as in the captions) for the words about the Son of Man coming in the glory of His Father; those words are in Matthew 16:27. Some phrases were garbled in the captions and are marked [unclear] (names near “the Taves and the Kers,” two places where a name appears to be missing around “punished,” and a word in Revelation 21:1). His remarks on immigration, lazy people being fed, eating blood, capital punishment and named members of the church are his own and are not verified here.

chunks.section_question: Why did Jesus come the first time, and what is the condemnation? (John 3:17-20)
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus’ first coming “was not to condemn the world” but to warn that a judgment is coming and to forgive and cleanse sin. He says those who do not believe are already condemned because light has come into the world and men loved darkness, because their deeds were evil.
chunks.text: Okay. Jesus’s first coming, as we know, was not to condemn the world. In John 3:17, but that the world through him might be saved. His first coming was not to judge the world. He come to warn the world there’s a judgment coming and, “My blood will forgive you your sins, clean you your sins, and you can correct all your wrongs. Your slate can be clean and you can be reconciled back to God.” That was his message. “He that believes on him is not condemned. He that believes not is condemned already, because he hasn’t believed on the name of the only begotten Son of God. And this is the condemnation: that light has come into the world, and men loved what? Darkness rather than light, because their deeds were what? Evil. For everyone that does evil hates the light.” Who’s the light? Jesus and his word. “Neither comes to the light.” Who’s the light? Jesus and his word. “Lest his deeds should what? Be exposed.”

chunks.section_question: Why do people reject the message, and when will the word judge us? (John 12:48, Acts 17:31)
chunks.short_answer: He says people who reject the message blame the preacher or the church, but the truth is “they want to sin and they don’t want anybody telling them they can’t.” He says the same word will judge us in the last day, that God has “an appointed day,” and that no one should rely on predicted dates.
chunks.text: You know, people that reject the message, they blame the preacher, they blame the church, they put the blame on everything. And the truth is, they want to sin and they don’t want anybody telling them they can’t. So they reject Christ because what? Christ is going to convict them of their sin so he can save them. And that’s why he came the first time. He didn’t come to back up that Old Testament law. But the second coming, John 12:48: “The word that I’ve have spoken to you, the same shall judge you” what? “In the last day.” Acts 17:31: he was a there was “He has appointed a day on which he will” what? scriptures.text_nkjv: He who rejects Me, and does not receive My words, has that which judges him—the word that I have spoken will judge him in the last day.
because He has appointed a day on which He will judge the world in righteousness by the Man whom He has ordained. He has given assurance of this to all by raising Him from the dead.”

chunks.section_question: Will believers appear before Christ, and is God partial? (2 Corinthians 5:10)
chunks.short_answer: He says “we will all appear before the judgment seat of Christ,” and that being a believer does not exempt you because Judas also believed, preached and cast out demons. He says many Christians think God would be partial to those who believe, and says that is “a lie.”
chunks.text: Second Corinthians 5:10: “We will all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.” How many of us? “But I’m a believer of Christ.” So what what? Judas was a believer of Christ too, you know. Have I got you thinking? Yeah, he believed in Christ. Is he in the lake of fire? Yes, he’s in the lake of fire. We don’t know our Bible. Did Judas preach the gospel? Yes. Did he cast out demons? Yes. Did he heal the sick? I mean, God healed the sick through him. Yeah. Are you there, church? You see, this thing is the power. This is the message of the gospel of Christ. This judgment is strong and it’s powerful and it moves us forward. We’re going to all appear. And and see, a lot of Christians don’t think they’re going to appear before Christ. They think God is partial because we believe in him. “Believed in you, Lord. I’m committing sexual immorality and doing everything this guy over here did, but he didn’t believe in you.” And and and so God says, “Well, he didn’t believe in me, I’m going to I’m going to mess him up. But you, you believe, all right.” Is God partial, folks? We’re lying to the people, and the people love to believe a lie.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to be judged by works? (Revelation 20:13, 2 Corinthians 5:10)
chunks.short_answer: He says they were judged each one according to their works, and that believing in Christ does not help a family if you abuse them, and does not help a sinner if you tell them they don’t have to turn. He says living for Christ helps our neighbors and families, and that grace and faith are not all there is to it.
chunks.text: “Anyway, that he may receive the things done when in this body according to what he has done, whether it be good or bad.” All right. “The sea gave up the dead who were in it. Death and Hades delivered up the dead who were in them. They were judged each one according to his” what? What’s the word? Works. See, it doesn’t do my wife and children any good I believe in Christ, and then I’m going out on my wife and I’m beating my kids to death because they do things that irritate me. And that doesn’t help them any. And I believe in Christ, and I tell the sinner, “You know, you just believe in Christ, you don’t have to turn from that.” Doesn’t help that sinner any or his home any. You see, us living for Christ is what helps our neighbor. That’s what helps our family. And now that’s a good place for a good amen. You may not agree with me, but that’s the key. And they got us thinking that this grace and faith is all there is to it. No, you can be a tremendous blessing in your home by following the word of God, and you can go to heaven.

chunks.section_question: Does Jesus come only once, and what is the new heaven and new earth? (Matthew 16:27, Revelation 21:1)
chunks.short_answer: He says the Bible nowhere says Jesus comes “once, twice, and the third time”; He comes one time, judges the world, resurrects the people, and then comes eternity. He says everything now will be “renovated by fire” and replaced by “a much better” heaven and earth, not surfing or fishing.
chunks.text: Matthew 16:20: “For the Son of Man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will reward every man according to his” what? Works. See, nowhere in the Bible does he say he’s coming once, twice, and the third time. It says he’s coming one time, and he’s going to judge the world, and he’s going to resurrect the people, and they’re going to stand before God, and then eternity. Revelations 21:1: “I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth [unclear] passed away. Also there was no more sea.” I love these young Christians when they say, “Boy, I can’t wait to catch that wave in heaven,” you know, surfing, or “Boy, just imagine the fishing in heaven.” and And I look at, I, you’re not getting this. Everything that you see here is going to be renovated by fire. It’s going to be burned up: buildings, everything’s gone, water gone, moon, stars, sun, everything’s gone, and a much better comes to replace it.

Now I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away. Also there was no more sea.

chunks.section_question: What will eternity be like? (Revelation 21:4-5, 2 Peter 3)
chunks.short_answer: He says God “will wipe every tear from their eyes,” there will be no more death, sorrow, crying or pain, because the former things have passed away, and God says “I make what? All things new.” He says the heavens will pass away with a great noise and a fervent heat, and that the new earth is “much better than what we know.”
chunks.text: Hallelujah. So get rid of those fairy tales. God has something much better than what we know. Now, “God will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death,” why? Cuz death is is conquered. Now, “no sorrow, no crying. There will be no more pain, for the former things have” what? Passed away. And remember, “with a fervent heat the heavens passed away with a great noise, the earth was burned up and everything in it.” And they want us down here on earth. Ain’t nothing to be down here for until he recreates the new earth. Hallelujah. I’m just throwing out some things to help you get through this nonsense out there. Then “he who sat on the throne said, ‘Behold, I make what? All things new.’” Wow. Fresh. Now I don’t know about you, but that sounds pretty good to me.

chunks.section_question: Will everyone get the same reward in heaven?
chunks.short_answer: He says there “are levels,” so what you do now depends on your reward; you will get eternal life, but people who do not pursue or grow in God will not get the same reward as those who do. He says the idea that everyone is treated equal is “the Disneyland gospel,” and that there are things to be rewarded up there.
chunks.text:
Is it worth living for Christ for 70 to 80 years on this earth to inherit an eternity like that? And we we already talked about Christ, you know, we get to love him and know him up there, and he’s the focus of everything, plus we get all the new heaven and a new earth to live in. There are levels, uh, so it’s important what you do now. Depends on your reward. These people think they all get the same reward. See, that’s just like these lazy people. They don’t want to work and they think they should be able to be fed and everything and drive cars just like the workers. And the Christians are like that, you know. We don’t pursue God, we don’t grow in God, yet we want the same reward that those who applied God, and it’s not there in the Bible. Now, you will get eternal life, don’t get me wrong, but remember there’s a new heaven and new earth, things are going on there’s a order up there, and I don’t know about you, but you want to be as high as you can when you get there. Amen.

You say, “Man, that sounds weird.” Yeah, I know, because we love the fair tale, the Disneyland gospel. We don’t want any responsibility or accountability to do anything, and we want everything handed to us, and it’s not that way. You will be judged according to your works. You see, Blake gets a very good paycheck because he has a good marketing uh skill to market, and see, you guys, want some of you want the same paycheck without putting the effort in, and it ain’t going to happen. But there’s things to be rewarded up there, and you want those rewards. Is that a good amen? Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: What is the message of the cross, and how should we respond? (Proverbs 20:11)
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus wants to keep us from “that lake of fire, that second death,” by choosing Him for forgiveness and starting to “start walking on the right road,” and going back to the cross when we fall. He says the message is “a total package”: forgiveness and cleansing plus a commitment to obey His word, with growth over time until we shine “by your good works, giving glory to God.”
chunks.text:
Young people, stop what you’re doing. Here, I love young people. They look at each other to see if this is cool or not. Young people, the Bible says, “Even a child is known by its ways, whether it is bad or whether it’s good.” And so we’ve got to choose to live the right way, and this is what the message is all about. Jesus wants to keep you from that lake of fire, that second death, and so he’s coming to tell you. You’re not looking at me. That’s it, sweetie, that beautiful face. I’d love to see those eyes. Do you understand when you do that you distract those around you? Yeah, they look to see what you’re doing. Adults do that. And see, a serious thing, our eternal life is on the line here, and we got to get enough respect to listen and soak it in and make a decision. And this is what I’m getting to.

Jesus is telling us to choose him for forgiveness for wrong and to start walking on the right road and start living for him. And if you fall, you go back to him, back to that cross, asked him to forgive and get back up on that road and keep walking. And you can reject it today. You can want to please your friends around you. You want to be the cool crowd. You can believe the lie. Adults can believe the lie that’s preached on radio and TV. I told you over the weekend that if Jesus Christ preached the message that preachers are preaching today, he would never have been crucified, because they are not warning you to turn from evil and do right and serve the living God. That’s why they killed him. They didn’t want to change, and religious people didn’t want to change. And so young people and adults this morning, this is the message of the cross. Are you going to choose not only the forgiveness of Christ and the cleansing of sin that he offers, but a commitment to obey his word and live for him? It’s a total package.

And let him slowly, you know, doesn’t have to be too slow now, but a lot of this doesn’t happen overnight. So when I’m telling you, some of you drag your feet way too long, but let him building. You keep getting back up. Keep letting him deal with it until that thing is gone. You just keep working on these things to finally you shine like a light in this world by your good works, giving glory to God.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Even a child is known by his deeds, Whether what he does is pure and right.

faqs.question: Who does he say goes to the lake of fire?
faqs.answer: He says cowards who do not stand up for Jesus, the unbelieving, the sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters and liars, if they do it “flagrantly and consistently,” will have their part in the lake that burns with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But the cowardly, unbelieving, abominable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.”

faqs.question: What does he mean by “the cowardly” in Revelation 21:8?
faqs.answer: He says it does not mean being afraid to drive on the freeway; it means not having “the courage of your faith” to stand up for what’s right and instead giving into the crowd, especially for teenagers who are peer pressured.

faqs.question: How does he say we grow spiritually?
faqs.answer: He says “get with people that are up there above you,” because “we get influenced by who we’re around and the quality of life that they have.”

faqs.question: What does he say about work and laziness?
faqs.answer: He says “no working, no eating” was the first law, and quotes the Proverb that a man’s stomach will drive him to work. He says letting people be lazy and still feeding them, or letting children stay at home to age 40, does not build self-esteem.

scriptures.text_nkjv: The person who labors, labors for himself, For his hungry mouth drives him on.

faqs.question: What does he say about eating blood?
faqs.answer: He says the command not to eat meat with the life blood was a “shadow law” of the blood of Christ, with no punishment attached. He says you can actually eat blood “if you don’t overdo it,” and it is used in many nations, like other parts of the animal.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But you shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood.

faqs.question: What does he say about marriage?
faqs.answer: He says marriage is “a public declaration” before God and people that you will be faithful, love that person, treat them right and raise your kids right. He says many people are “just shacking up,” but “Christians get married.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.

faqs.question: Whose fault does he say it is when evil happens?
faqs.answer: He says it is not God’s fault but ours, because God gave human beings the responsibility to “take care of the criminal” and judge. He says he gets tired of people blaming God and “his perfect word when it is our fault.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Surely for your lifeblood I will demand a reckoning; from the hand of every beast I will require it, and from the hand of man. From the hand of every man’s brother I will require the life of man. “Whoever sheds man’s blood, By man his blood shall be shed; For in the image of God He made man.

faqs.question: What does he say about immigrants and the law?
faqs.answer: He says “we’re to allow immigrants into our nation, but they should come in the legal way,” because it is not fair to those who came legally. He says government leaders who do not back up the law are “wimps.”

faqs.question: Who does he say is supposed to punish criminals?
faqs.answer: He says civil leaders, not the church, are supposed to deal with criminals and carry out punishment by death, and says “they’re not doing it.” He says the church’s greatest punishment is excommunication.

faqs.question: Why did Jesus not judge the world at His first coming?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus came to warn that a judgment is coming and to offer forgiveness and a clean slate through His blood, and that those who do not believe “condemned already.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but that the world through Him might be saved. “He who believes in Him is not condemned; but he who does not believe is condemned already, because he has not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God. And this is the condemnation, that the light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For everyone practicing evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds should be exposed.

faqs.question: What does he say about Judas?
faqs.answer: He says Judas “believed in Christ,” preached, cast out demons and healed the sick through God’s power, yet “he’s in the lake of fire,” to show that believing alone does not exempt anyone from judgment.

faqs.question: What does he say about grace and faith being all there is to it?
faqs.answer: He says “they got us thinking that this grace and faith is all there is to it,” and that following the word of God is what makes you a blessing to your home and takes you to heaven.

faqs.question: What does he say about surfing and fishing in heaven?
faqs.answer: He says everything here “is going to be renovated by fire” and replaced by something “much better than what we know,” so people should get rid of those “fairy tales.”

faqs.question: Why does he say living for Christ is worth it?
faqs.answer: He asks if it is “worth living for Christ for 70 to 80 years on this earth to inherit an eternity like that,” where we get to love and know Him and have a new heaven and new earth.

faqs.question: What does he say about preachers today?
faqs.answer: He says if Jesus preached the message that preachers are preaching today “he would never have been crucified,” because they do not warn people to turn from evil.
